leads.title: Sachem Capital Corp. discloses unserved $1.9 billion complaint seeking to unwind IRG Global property-contribution transaction
leads.why: Sachem Capital Corp.'s Nov. 16, 2026 10-Q discloses that an unnamed party filed a complaint (not yet served on the company as of the filing date) seeking compensatory damages the complaint itself estimates at not less than $1.9 billion, plus an injunction against consummation of a 'Transaction' involving the contribution, transfer or encumbrance of properties, avoidance of that transfer, appointment of a receiver, and a constructive trust over the transferred assets. This appears tied to Sachem's disclosed Industrial Realty Group Global, LLC transaction (a separate July 2026 California suit by 17 plaintiffs already sought to enjoin the same deal pending arbitration). The dollar figure and real-property-contribution/receiver/constructive-trust relief sought make this a potentially significant CRE-adjacent securities/transaction dispute, but the SEC excerpt alone does not name the plaintiff, court, or docket -- newsroom should identify the actual complaint (likely via the IRG Global transaction or a related state/federal docket) before writing it up, and should separately note the figure looks large relative to Sachem's own balance sheet, which may mean it is an outlier claim rather than a realistic exposure estimate.

leads.title: Clark County, Nevada formally appeals $12M+ Badlands golf course property-tax 'taking' judgment to Nevada Supreme Court
leads.why: News3LV and KTNV (Las Vegas) report that Clark County commissioners voted, with no discussion, to appeal to the Nevada Supreme Court a district court ruling that found the county unlawfully 'took' property taxes on the former Badlands golf course land (owned by developer Yohan Lowie's entities) after courts had already ruled the City of Las Vegas illegally took that same land -- News3LV headlines the judgment at $12M, KTNV's reporting cites a roughly $12.4M-$13M county bill with interest accruing over $3,000/day, and News3LV separately reports the county formally filed its notice of appeal 'this week' after the commissioner vote. This is the latest turn in the long-running, high-profile Badlands litigation (the city separately settled its own Badlands claims for $636 million per Lowie's attorney) and would be a notable, geographically underrepresented (Nevada) property-tax-assessment/inverse-condemnation-adjacent matter if a source can confirm the vote/filing date -- a WebSearch-only environment with no page-fetch access could not open either article to confirm the exact date (searches returned it among 2026 results but a specific day was not visible in the snippets); newsroom should confirm the filing date before publishing and decide whether this continues an entity/story already in js/data.js (a search of the tracker for 'Badlands'/'Gypsum Resources'/'Yohan Lowie' by this run found none, so it would likely be a new matter, category zoning-land-use or eminent-domain, parties Clark County/Yohan Lowie-affiliated entity/City of Las Vegas).
